description:
Redundant Indexes — SCH0003

Flags indexes whose column list is a leftmost prefix of (or equal to) another index of the same table: they serve no lookup the wider index cannot, while every write maintains them and they occupy buffer pool and disk. A UNIQUE index is never reported as covered by a non-unique one, PRIMARY is never the redundant side, FULLTEXT/SPATIAL indexes only compare with their own kind, and InnoDB's implicit primary-key suffix on secondary indexes is taken into account ((a, pk) is redundant with (a)). All redundant indexes on a server are reported in a single SCH0003 finding per run, with one DROP INDEX remediation each. Wire v4 (indexes on the schema snapshot).

prerequisites.description: Schema index metadata must be monitored (monitoring-schema-indexes=true) — without it the snapshot carries no indexes and this check reports nothing

config_keys.label: Mask schema/table/index names
config_keys.help: Partially obscure schema, table, index and column names in the finding (e.g. "window" -> "wi???ow") and drop the DROP INDEX statements, so the log entry is not directly useful to someone who only has log access (PCI-DSS style deployments).
